subject: 06:35 offline T1 bank independently verified; generation complete
body:
# Orchard morning handoff

Latest review: 06:35 Europe/London, 2 October 2026. Overnight supervision remains authorised until 07:30. This records the current result, not completion of the whole Expeditions build.

## Main result

The offline Four Locks Tier 1 bank is complete: 64 distinct certified missions plus a separate certified fallback. All four archetypes are represented, with 16 river, 16 islands, 18 hedges and 14 terraces topology fingerprints and 25 Sudoku dependency patterns. Each accepted mission has two distinct production Common squads, different output plans and a real winning prepared-alcove route. Independent production reducer replay and deterministic reconstruction passed all 40 targeted checks in the final bank suite.

Manifest: docs/expeditions/v2/certification/four-locks/displaced-v1/bank-manifest.json.
Final delivery: docs/expeditions/v2/reports/codex-C-08B-displaced-bank-21-24.md.

This is generatorVersion 2, using the explicitly versioned displaced construction packet. Runtime still exposes only the previous generatorVersion 1 private river Tier 1 reference. No bank import, version migration, integrated App playthrough or QA-01 approval has occurred. T1 bank generation stopped at completeness; four final candidate slots were unused. The manifest retains 31 bounded unknown records without retries or false impossibility claims.

## Other verified work

- Default Four Locks Tiers 1–5 each have individual mathematical and tactical reference proofs. This does not complete higher-tier banks. Lower-band and one-Legendary/two-Common exclusions have exact printed-stat assignment checks.
- All five mathematical hooks have production and engine integration tests. Only Four Locks has full mission references; other-family packets remain gated on QA-01.
- Advanced Sudoku generation satisfies the specified Tier 4 pair/intersection and Tier 5 pair/causal cage-chain requirements on proved samples. Basic hashes and existing default certificates remain pinned. Advanced pattern diversity is still incomplete.
- A separate native-cage experiment passed its strict gate tests but yielded no qualifying puzzle in its bounded 16-request comparison. It remains offline and stopped; it did not improve accepted yield or replace defaults.
- Crossing displacement is implemented in the separate offline packet, with independent path/cut/reserved-footprint checks and full entity/schema/reducer evidence. Defaults were preserved.
- Six UI checks independently passed: geometry, camera, private mount gating and exact combat/stat feedback strings. Hint text is in the puzzle drawer; engine-updated output choices synchronise in source. No real integrated UI acceptance is implied.
- The imported art package contains 49 assets, all 30 production hero idles and additional first-slice poses. Five art/package checks independently passed. Bushel rear, Tuppence exhausted and Dapple exhausted repaired QA sheets were independently inspected across four backgrounds and three scales. Live ground anchors, contrast and state readability remain pending. Dapple action uses an explicit idle fallback; distorted painted plinths remain withheld.
- Core review findings R-01 through R-05 and certificate R-06 have passing regression evidence. R-07 remains open: the external planner counts denied spends in its used metric. Source inspection shows denied calls return before reducer execution; reported overages are not evidence of extra admitted transitions. All batch requests retained their 8,000-state limits and warnings.
- Desktop performance evidence was reviewed, not independently rerun: p95 reconstruction 18.556ms, preview 1.0138ms and reducer 0.5245ms. No tablet, browser, full-bundle or bounded-memory acceptance.

## Next work, in order

1. Claude C-06A/C-09: read the mailbox, wire the already published generator/hooks and controller/profile component into the exact private App route. Start with the existing version 1 certified reference; the offline version 2 bank needs a deliberate reviewed regeneration/migration handoff. Confirm integrated save/resume, owned cards and atomic first-clear/replay rewards. Full build/regression/smoke requires the final-build mailbox lock.
2. Claude C-08A: repair R-07 budget accounting with bounded regression evidence. Retain unknown search semantics and the real reducer as the only simulation authority.
3. Codex C-05/C-06B/C-10: capture and review the real private slice, including instructions, all printed-stat effects, ability hands, previews/results, scrolling/zoom and art alignment. Do not infer this from mathematical/replay tests.
4. Scrum QA-01: review the integrated Four Locks slice. Other four family packets remain waiting until this gate is satisfied.
5. Codex C-03/C-08B: review and integrate version 2 bank reconstruction only after its interface/version acceptance; complete higher-tier banks and their genuine diversity. The completed T1 packet does not complete C-08B overall.
6. Both QA-02: demonstrate all 25 family/tier combinations, better-card progression and meaningful contribution from every printed stat. Device and child tests remain unavailable: five-minute duration, comprehension, enjoyment and Android/tablet layout are unverified.

## Coordination

Codex builder chat: 01a0f955-b5c7-72f0-852c-34a13fc6c5d2, title Build Ninefold Orchard Expeditions v. It is idle after completing the bank and releasing C-08B. No new generation follow-up was sent after completeness. No locks at inspection.

Claude is external; activity is unknown. Its latest report is 23:35 on 1 October and 24 local handoffs remain unread. The mailbox cannot wake it. Do not launch a duplicate process, claim it is coding or overwrite its files. On return it should read its inbox before editing. One writer per file remains mandatory.

Private eudaimon/Rooke access, printed-stat progression and three-star first family/tier rewards remain unchanged. No deployment, public release, destructive cleanup or paid service is authorised. Detailed evidence, message acknowledgements and dispatch history are in scrum-overnight-status.md.
